svg.title: Run 1 records the dead end. Run 2 uses the receipt before selection.
svg.desc: Three lanes on one synthetic case, with one diagnostic read per call. The memoryless control repeats inspect_pipeline on three calls and stays 3 of 3 unresolved. Run 1 starts with empty history and four options. Decider 2B chooses inspect_pipeline, spends one read, and ends unresolved. One inference, 21.6 s client time. The deterministic verifier stores a disposition_unchanged Decision Receipt. Run 1 is not saved. Run 2 is a new call with an exact receipt match. Before the first Decider request and before any read, the controller precludes only inspect_pipeline. This block spends no read and no inference. The three remaining diagnostics retain their original order. The same Decider 2B makes one fresh choice, inspect_schema_keys, spends one read and completes with a verified repair in 26.6 s client time. No second Decider call. The receipt has exact negative authority, Decider chooses, and the verifier owns truth. The private AWS roles sit underneath. Measured comparison only: superseded post-choice Run 2 used 54.8 s and 2 inferences, optimized Run 2 uses 26.6 s and 1 inference. Observed Run 2 client latency fell 28.2 s, or 51.4%. n = 1, same synthetic case, each proof once. No dollar savings measured.

text.font-family: Iowan Old Style, Palatino, Georgia, serif

g.text: Run 1 records the dead end. Run 2 uses it. The same Decider 2B chooses every tool.
